What this translates to is that they are strong, fast, and quiet.

And if you have more slots for case fans than your MOBO has SYS FAN headers, then do not fret - these fans have the ability to daisy chain so you can run multiple through a single header. You plug the 4 pin connector into the header, and then you daisy chain another fan's 4 pin connector into the branching 3 pin connector of the first fan. The 3 pin daisy chain connector has the second fan run at the same RPM that the first fan connected directly to the header runs at. Excellent feature in addition to all the other aforementioned stats.

I see comments about folks hating the shape but I have it on a shelf above my TV in my living room on top of a fan to keep it cool and I don't notice it unless I'm looking for it. It has so many more features than the old one that I'm still figuring them out. I like that it has MAC filtering to block out unknown MAC addresses. I'm still figuring out the built in VPN option. I'm so glad I bought this thing a bit more than a month ago now.

I have been printing every day for over a month with no issues.  The included equipment such as the build plate, AMS, and sample filament are terrific and simple to begin.  My only complaint is the inclusion of PLA-CF filament.  This stuff is a little too brittle and rough on the AMS right out of the box. reviews.author: Stang99x
reviews.body: I previously bought and used another model of printer.  We'll call it a model 3 V2. (and those who know anything about 3D printer will know what that is)  It was the most frustrating thing ever with constant spaghetti issues, failing about 9 of 10 attempts to print even with glue.  As such I pretty much canned the idea of 3D printing.  And then one day I saw an ad for this Bambu labs printer.  Yes, it is pricey with the AMS on top.  But this printer is the shizzizznit.  From the minute I fired it up it has worked  nearly flawlessly.  And I have had it running almost constantly for several weeks.  The only issues I had were related to tightening a few belt screws and lubricating the screws.  I've had maybe 5 failed jobs out of 100.  I couldn't get 5 successful jobs in a 100 with the last one I had.  Anyone who says something degrading about this printer is either comparing it to a commercial unit or just isn't cut out for this stuff.  The software alone is light years better for the average user.  No more slicing and editing to get it right.  The Bambu software handles the job itself.  I do wish there was a little more in regards to optional printing methods but I wouldn't trade this for anything else.  The AMS can at times be aggravating but for the most part once it is setup you can forget it and just print.  If you can spring for this, you will not be disappointed.

reviews.body: Neat little case that can pack in a motherlode of components, and has all sides perforated except the front, so great cooling. Just be sure to mount your PSU where the original HDD mount plate is, so it will get fresh air from the side and eject hot air out the top, and not mess with the airflow over the rest of the case.

reviews.author: Jokr
reviews.body: An awesome and well-designed microATX case that supports a wide range of parts.  Building with the case is quite easy but may take some preplanning depending on the parts you use.  I later upgraded to a AIO 360 with a thick radiator and ran into some clearance issues with the RAM when trying to top mount it, so I ended up mounting it to the side using the included bracket.  I also am using an SFX PSU and the CPU power cable was a tad too short to have the PSU mounted at the front of the case, but the case supports swapping the side mounted SSD bracket and front mounted PSU bracket location which resolved my issue.  It ended up working out as now the PSU can intake air from the side mesh panel.  One issue with the case is that the front panel is a solid body so there is no way to add air intake from the front, but the wood panel version of this case which was released later includes ventilation.

reviews.author: Dso4
reviews.body: I needed a small form facter case for my girlfriend's build since she rents a small room and I don't want her new pc to take up too much space. I bought this on sale at 72 bucks and it has been great to build in. It came with instructions that are fully drawn out and demonstrate different variations of build for different components and use cases. The screws are alao very organized in a plastic container with dividers. With this case, I was able to spend under 80 dollars and still get a quality case with USB C front panel as well as a small form factor, without having to shell out over 100 dollars on an ITX case, meaning I can also save money going with an MATX case vs am ITX one.

reviews.author: Ajay B
reviews.body: Great build quality, ample room for large gpus and different components, and many configurations to fit parts. The temps on my Hellhound 9070 xt don't exceed 60 degrees Celsius and the cpu doesn't exceed 50. I can fit a multiple hard drives as well.

reviews.author: KneelbfMC
reviews.body: Love this case! Perfect size, everything fits (within reason) and has lots of cable management tied downs and areas to hide them. Just have to plan out the build a bit more versus a normal ATX case. I can absolutely recommend this, you will not be disappointed.

reviews.author: Eternifity
reviews.body: There is so much space and so many fan slottings its genuinely insane. I have fit some ridiculous things in this case and gotten equally ridiculous performance as a result. You can theoretically put 3x360mm in a custom loop in here, which is bananas. The only downsides are some oversights. The front panel cables have no routing/protection and tend to be smushed by a bottom 360mm radiator. It's 2025 so I feel this could be fixed by having an angled outlet for front panel cables from their respective daughterboards. Another cable routing issue is the PC power plug extension running through the case.Given that the bottom of the case only supports a 360mm radiator, I feel like the cable should have been routed along the bottom, as having it on the top lets 280mm radiators smush against it. The system that is used to allow for the PSU and 2.5 drives to relocate is VERY underutilized. Both sides of the case where this system is used is being enough to support an entire 160mm fan for example. Providing an STL for 3D printing would be nice, I may do it myself. However, mounting said possible 160mm fan on the front would yields a problem, as the front of the case is unexplainably solid with no possibility for usage for air flow.

Online reviews seem to say it's not necessary to use this GCC update - Windows should automatically find things, or you can always manually download. reviews.author: JoeBloe
reviews.body:
I dual-boot Windows and Linux on two separate storage devices, and the BIOS consistently only lists one of these devices when I go into the menu that sets up boot order prioritization. My PC will also sometimes hang on reboot. This happened a few days ago when I attempted to enter BIOS flashing mode, which resulted in a persistent boot failure that I could only fix by clearing the CMOS multiple times. The board couldn't even perform a POST. I only got the 0d error message, which is pretty generic.

I thought that these issues would be cleared up after a few BIOS updates, but they kept lingering. In retrospect, I wish I had gone with a different model. I've been building for nearly 30 years in both personal and professional settings, and this has been the glitchiest board I've ever used. I think it's telling that they've released over a dozen BIOS updates for this thing in less than a year (some are no longer listed because they were betas).

reviews.author: Gamer67
reviews.body:
Worst MB I have ever used. I’ve yet to get it boot consistently. When it does boot, it often freezes randomly and I have to hard reset it. It’s just not a stable platform right now, even after updating all the drivers and bios.

Currently have a 9900X installed and some Corsair DDR5, got it all as a bundle. Half the time I hit the power button the CPU/DRAM lights are on indicating no CPU/RAM, so I check everything, reseat the processor…..nothing. Make sure I hear the click of the RAM….nope. Finally figure out you have to push the ram in even harder, so that’s a thing. Even after that “problem” was solved I still cannot get it to boot consistently. Honestly, I would avoid this MB and go for any other 870E.

reviews.author: N. K.
reviews.body: This is my first MSI motherboard, and I'm happy with it. It has all the USB connections I need at the appropriate speeds, including two USB4 Thunderbolt ports. It also has an S/PDIF port, critical to my audio setup. I like how easy it is to install M.2 drives, particularly in slot M2_4. It has great connectivity, too, with support for Wi-Fi 7 and Blutooth 5.4, plus a 5G Ethernet port. I have this motherboard supporting a 9950X3D and 64GB of DDR5 RAM, and it does so without issue. I also like that updating the BIOS wasn't too difficult. Overall, this motherboard meets all my needs. If I had to complain about one thing, I wish the RGB controls played better with third-party apps. But that's about it.
